clue.text: Chatter to the French film star

parts.note: to chatter idly is to gab
le is the French masculine word for 'the'

explanation.surface: Someone gossips away to a French movie celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: Clark Gable was a Hollywood leading man of the 1930s and 40s.
explanation.definitionFit: Clark Gable was a famous Hollywood actor, an example of a screen star.

clue.text: Order goalie not to scorn assistance

indicators.note: order, as an instruction to arrange, means the letters are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A manager tells the keeper to refuse any help.
explanation.definitionFit: To act independently, refusing help from others, is the idiom meaning act solo.

clue.text: Stick — at the crease?

explanation.surface: Someone asks if the stick belongs on the cricket pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the crease is the batsman's line; a batsman at the crease is still batting, so can 'bat on'.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a short rod, like a relay runner's; a batsman still in can carry on batting.

clue.text: Seeing crew about agreement

indicators.note: about means around, so the crew wraps the agreement

parts.note: a rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen
yes is a word of agreement

explanation.surface: A rowing team witnesses a deal being struck.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the faculty of vision, the power of sight.

clue.text: Seek food, ammunition and military attire

parts.note: to forage is to search about for provisions
a cap is a small percussion charge, as in a cap gun

explanation.surface: A soldier's kit list: find rations, gather bullets, put on the uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A forage cap is a soldier's peaked undress headgear, so an item of army clothing.

clue.text: Said to turn out right

indicators.note: said signals that the word is spoken, so a word sounding the same is entered

parts.note: to fare is how things turn out, as in 'how did you fare?'

explanation.surface: It is claimed things will end up correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair means just or equitable, as in a fair decision.

clue.text: Herd straying — straying as a result of this?

definitions.text: Herd straying — straying as a result of this?

indicators.note: straying means wandering out of place, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: straying means going wrong, erring

explanation.surface: Cattle wander off, misled by a false lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'straying' does two jobs in turn: the first is the anagram signal on HERD, giving REDH; the second supplies ERRING.
explanation.definitionFit: A misleading distraction that sends investigators off course, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Blimp — he'll prattle on

explanation.surface: A pompous colonel who talks endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: Colonel Blimp was a cartoon pompous British officer, but here a blimp is an airship.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasbag is an airship's gas container; it is also slang for a chatterer.

clue.text: Yards used with fashionable suit

parts.note: courts are enclosed yards
hip means trendy

explanation.surface: Lots of fabric needed for a trendy outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like clothing measured in yards; it is the old sense of wooing.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay suit to someone is to woo them, so wooing is the sense.

clue.text: Name for a copper

explanation.surface: What to call a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a police officer; here it is a bronze coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Penny is a girl's name; a penny is a small coin made of copper or bronze.

clue.text: Horn is imminent

explanation.surface: A car horn is about to sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A horn belongs to an orchestra's wind section; something coming soon is said to be brewing, in that idiom.

clue.text: Turn down, right, having turned about

indicators.note: about here means going around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: having turned, as in spun round, gives spun

explanation.surface: Instructions for a manoeuvre: go down, then right, then turn round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn down' looks like a direction to steer; it means reject. 'about' puts SPUN around R.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn down an offer is to reject it scornfully.

clue.text: A loose member of the family

parts.note: to loose a knot is to undo or untie it

explanation.surface: A relative who has gone off the rails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' reads as an adjective for a wayward relative, but it is the verb, to undo.
explanation.definitionFit: Auntie is an affectionate word for a parent's sister, a relative.

clue.text: Hair-splitting chap interrupts to criticise essay

indicators.note: the chap breaks into the middle of the next word, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly, as a reviewer does
Ed is a man's name, a typical crossword chap
an essay is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: A fussy man breaks in to find fault with a student's essay.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantry is excessive concern with minor detail, which is what hair-splitting means.

clue.text: Corporation open tomb in error

indicators.note: in error suggests these letters are muddled and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A company digs up a grave by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' is the old jokey sense of a pot belly, not a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Embonpoint is plumpness of figure; corporation is dated slang for a big belly.

clue.text: Having started wide of the target

explanation.surface: An archer whose first shot misses.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman or runner who has begun scoring is off the mark; a shot that misses is also off the mark.

clue.text: Leading seaman's not passed on

parts.note: leading means first
a hand is a crew member on a ship

explanation.surface: A senior sailor has not died yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passed on' suggests dying; it means relayed through others.
explanation.definitionFit: Information obtained directly, not via others, is direct experience.

clue.text: A writer, would you say?

indicators.note: say here signals that the word is to be spoken, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: 'sure' is the agreeing reply to a 'would you?' request

explanation.surface: A question: would you call this person an author?
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic accent 'sure' and the playwright's name sound much the same.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw was an Irish playwright and critic, an example of an author.

clue.text: Caribbean islands in conflict and they are victorious

parts.note: WI is the abbreviation for the West Indies

indicators.note: in conflict suggests the words are at odds and jumbled

explanation.surface: Island nations at war, and they come out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in conflict' rearranges AND THEY to NTHEDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevail in a contest is to triumph, the idiom of succeeding.

clue.text: There are thousands around set to help-farm worker

indicators.note: the thousands go round the set, one piece surrounding another

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, twice for thousands
ilk means kind or type, a set
aid means help

explanation.surface: Many people help out at a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A milkmaid is a woman who milks cows on a farm.

clue.text: Depicted in the crudest colour

indicators.note: the colour is shown within the run of these words, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A shade portrayed in the roughest painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecru is a pale greyish-yellow shade, like unbleached linen.

clue.text: Evangelist and soldier left quietly in poem

parts.note: John is one of the four Gospel writers
GI is an American private soldier
p (piano) is the musical instruction to play quietly
taken as written

explanation.surface: A saint and a soldier slip away in a piece of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The poem is William Cowper's comic ballad of a runaway horse ride.
explanation.definitionFit: William Cowper's comic ballad about a draper's runaway ride bears this title.

clue.text: Land, on fire

explanation.surface: Territory ablaze.
explanation.definitionFit: To alight is to descend and settle; alight also means burning.

clue.text: Open late, perhaps, for the supply of chamois

indicators.note: perhaps suggests these letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A shop keeping late hours to stock leather cloths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chamois' suggests the polishing leather; here it is the goat-like mountain animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The chamois is a goat-antelope of the Alps, so a definition by example.

clue.text: There are a lot of Indians here a crowd turned up

definitions.text: There are a lot of Indians here

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a mass is a crowd

explanation.surface: A large gathering of people arrives in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is a populous state of north-east India.

clue.text: Short play originally starring Jack as an executor

indicators.note: originally means taking just the opening of the word that follows

parts.note: Jack Ketch was a notorious 17th-century English public executioner

explanation.surface: A brief drama whose leading role is a hangman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executor' looks like the legal term for someone handling a will; here it is someone who executes, a hangman.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief comic scene in a revue is a short piece of theatre.

clue.text: Leaders of the Establishment never embraced this dogma

indicators.note: leaders of the following words means taking each opening letter

explanation.surface: Establishment figures never accepted this doctrine.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle held as true, a doctrine.

clue.text: Old painter put up unfinished

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means written from bottom to top, so read backwards
unfinished means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: Edgar Degas was a French Impressionist painter

explanation.surface: An elderly artist was hung but not completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reverses DEGA (DEGAS 'unfinished') to give AGED.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged means elderly, having lived a long time.

clue.text: Gave information about money, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: to sing is criminals' ... for informing to the police, so sang
L, from Latin libra, stands for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: Someone informed the police about some cash, in a way.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is informal vocabulary, one particular way of talking.

clue.text: An East Riding misspelling for 'thorough'

indicators.note: a misspelling puts letters in the wrong order, so these are rearranged

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire dialect spelling of a common word.
explanation.walkthrough: The East Riding was a division of Yorkshire in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ingrained is deep-rooted and complete, as in an ingrained habit.

clue.text: Considered state old-fashioned about it

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the next word wraps the following one

parts.note: something old-fashioned is dated
taken as written

explanation.surface: A view that a statement is behind the times.
explanation.definitionFit: To meditate is to think deeply about something, to ponder.

clue.text: Spotted bananas

explanation.surface: Fruit with dark patches on its skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotty means covered in dots, and also slightly mad, as 'bananas' means crazy.
